level1.text: The refractive index of a soap film is $1.33$, and at one point its thickness is $420\,\text{nm}$. Light arrives at normal incidence on the film. What is the path difference between the waves reflected from the two surfaces of the film? Give your answer in nanometres.
The wavelength of red laser light in air is $633\,\text{nm}$. What is the wavelength of the light in magnesium fluoride, whose refractive index is $1.38$?

An $\text{MgF}_2$ coating ($n = 1.38$) is evaporated onto the glass of a camera lens so that light of wavelength $500\,\text{nm}$ is reflected as little as possible. The refractive index of the glass is $1.52$, and the light arrives at normal incidence. How thick is the thinnest such coating?

The refractive index of a soap film is $1.33$, and there is air on both sides of it. Light arrives at normal incidence on the film. How thick is the thinnest film that reflects light of wavelength $600\,\text{nm}$ most strongly?

The refractive index of the plastic of a spectacle lens is $1.60$. At normal incidence a single-layer anti-reflection coating would cancel the reflection completely if the waves reflected from its two surfaces were equally strong. What should the refractive index of the coating then be?

level2.text: The thickness of a soap film ($n = 1.33$) is $240\,\text{nm}$ at one point, and there is air on both sides of it. White light arrives at normal incidence on the film. Which wavelength of visible light ($400$–$700\,\text{nm}$) is missing from the reflected light?

A glass lens ($n = 1.52$) has a $110\,\text{nm}$ thick $\text{MgF}_2$ coating ($n = 1.38$) on its surface. Light arrives at normal incidence on the coating. For which wavelength of visible light ($400$–$700\,\text{nm}$) is the reflection from the coating weakest?

An $\text{MgF}_2$ coating ($n = 1.38$) is made on glass ($n = 1.52$) so that it reflects light of wavelength $520\,\text{nm}$ as little as possible at normal incidence. The manufacturer wants a layer thicker than the thinnest possible. How thick is the second thinnest coating that reflects this wavelength most weakly?

In a beam splitter a thin titanium dioxide layer is made on glass ($n = 1.52$) so that it reflects light of wavelength $550\,\text{nm}$ as much as possible. Assume that the refractive index of the layer is $2.30$ and that the light arrives from air at normal incidence on the layer. How thick is the thinnest such layer?

level3.text:
A soap film ($n = 1.33$) made in a vertical wire frame is lit with the yellow light of a sodium lamp, with wavelength $589\,\text{nm}$, arriving at normal incidence on the film.

Gravity thins the film at the top, and the topmost part of the film looks black. Below it bright and dark horizontal bands alternate, and the film gets thicker downwards.

How thick is the film at the second dark band, when the topmost black region is not counted as a band?

A camera objective has four separate glass lenses, that is, eight surfaces at which light passes from air into glass or from glass into air. Each surface is coated so that it reflects $1.3\,\%$ of the light arriving at it at normal incidence.

Assume that the glass does not absorb light and that light reflected once no longer reaches the sensor.

What percentage of the light entering the objective gets through it?

A soap film ($n = 1.33$) is in air, and white light arrives at normal incidence on the film. In the visible range the film reflects most strongly the wavelengths $630\,\text{nm}$ and $450\,\text{nm}$, and there are no other strongly reflected wavelengths between them. How thick is the film?
